To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most prevalent INH resistance mutations in clinical M. tuberculosis isolates are in the katG gene, and that INH resistance mutations occur at different frequencies in different geographic regions.

(1) INH resistance in Mtb isolates was mainly associated with mutations in the katG gene, followed by mutations in the oxyR-ahp C region, and mutations in the inh A promoter region; (2) the most frequent mutation in the katG 463 gene was Ser315Thr, followed by Ser315Tyr; (3) the most frequent mutations in the oxy R-ahp C intergenic region were G-15T and A-16G;
the majority of INH resistance mutations are in katG and inhA genes, and that the majority of the INH resistance mutations in katG gene are in Ser315 codon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular characterization of the mutations associated with isonicotinic acid hydrazide resistance in M. tuberculosis isolates from China.
the molecular characteristics of mutations associated with the isoniazid (INH) resistance in Mycobacteria.
the molecular characterization of mutations associated to isoniazid (INH) resistance in Mycobacterial isolates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the majority of the INH-resistant isolates in our region have a mutation in katG gene.
mutations at the katG463 codon, the inhA promoter region, the mabA-inhAC intergenic region, the iniBAC region and the efpA region are all associated with INH resistance.
the present work has shown that mutations in the katG, inhA and oxyR-ahp operon genes are associated with isoniaid resistance in M. tuberculosis isolates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the importance of the molecular analysis of the katG gene for the diagnosis of INH resistance in clinical M. tuberculosis isolates.
we have developed a novel method to identify and quantify the amount of a specific protein in a cell.
we are developing a novel approach to identify and characterize the genetic determinants of resistance in M. tuberculosis, using a combination of biochemistry and genetics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many different ways to be drug resistant in M. tuberculosis.
there is no one gene that can predict the resistance profile of M. tuberculosis to the first-line anti-TB drugs.

the molecular characterization of INH-resistance associated mutations is essential for the understanding the molecular basis of the drug resistance in M.tuberculosis and to develop rapid molecular diagnostic methods for the detection of the drug resistance.
